title: Global Differential Geometry
notes: Open by placing the chapter after the local theory of surfaces. The lecture asks what survives when small curvature measurements are accumulated over an entire surface, and why compactness, completeness, and topology force restrictions that no coordinate chart can see alone.

title: From Local Data To A Global Ledger
notes: Use the ledger metaphor carefully. Gaussian curvature, geodesic curvature, corner turning, and vector-field rotation are local readings, but integration and compactness make them global quantities. The aim is to show how these local readings balance against Euler characteristic.

title: Compact Surfaces Make Curvature Finite
notes: Stress that compactness is not merely a topological adjective here. It guarantees finite total area for smooth metrics, makes continuous curvature attain extrema, and prevents curvature contributions from escaping to an end. That is why closed surfaces support clean integral identities.

title: Gauss-Bonnet With Boundary
notes: Present the formula as an accounting identity for a region. Interior Gaussian curvature, boundary geodesic curvature, and corner exterior angles combine to produce a purely topological number. Each term can change under deformation, but the total remains fixed.

title: Closed Surfaces: Curvature Reads Genus
notes: For a closed oriented surface, all boundary terms vanish and Gauss-Bonnet becomes a direct bridge from geometry to topology. The sphere, torus, and higher genus examples are not just illustrations; they show that the sign of average curvature is constrained by genus.

title: Triangulation As A Sanity Check
notes: Use the triangulated surface to connect smooth curvature to angle defect. On a fine mesh, the sum of vertex defects approximates the smooth integral of K dA. Euler characteristic appears because the same counting identity underlies both curvature defect and combinatorial topology.

title: Geodesic Curvature Is The Boundary Payment
notes: A geodesic boundary contributes no geodesic curvature, so the interior curvature and corner terms must carry the whole topological charge. On a spherical cap, the boundary circle usually is not a geodesic, and its turning exactly compensates the cap area.

title: Index Ideas: Turning Of A Field
notes: Introduce index as a rotation count made intrinsic by a moving orthonormal frame. Away from zeros the field has a well-defined angle, and around a zero the angle can wind. Poincare-Hopf says the total winding is forced by topology.

title: A Local Frame Reveals Curvature
notes: The connection form measures how a tangent frame turns under parallel transport. Its exterior derivative is curvature area. Integrating around a small loop therefore compares boundary rotation with enclosed curvature, which is the infinitesimal engine behind Gauss-Bonnet and index formulas.

title: Completeness Turns Geodesics Into Global Tools
notes: Move from compact surfaces to complete metrics. Hopf-Rinow lets geodesics exist for all time and realizes distances by minimizing geodesics. This changes local geodesic equations into global comparison tools for cut loci, shortest loops, and covering maps.

title: Jacobi Fields Detect Conjugate Points
notes: Explain Jacobi fields as separation vectors between nearby geodesics. On a surface, the scalar equation j double prime plus K j equals zero shows how curvature focuses or defocuses geodesic families. Conjugate points record the failure of geodesic variation to remain locally minimizing.

title: Hadamard: Nonpositive Curvature Unwraps
notes: The Hadamard principle is the chapter's cleanest global upgrade. Completeness prevents geodesics from ending, simple connectivity removes deck ambiguity, and nonpositive curvature prevents conjugate focusing. Together these conditions make the exponential map a global coordinate system.

title: Total Curvature Of Curves
notes: Pause to show a one-dimensional global phenomenon inside the surface chapter. The integral of curvature along a closed space curve controls how much the tangent direction must sweep on the unit sphere. This gives obstruction-style information that is invisible from any short arc.

title: Flat And Developable Models
notes: Use flat surfaces to separate intrinsic geometry from embedding intuition. A plane, cylinder, and flat torus can all have zero Gaussian curvature intrinsically, yet their global identifications and embeddings behave differently. Curvature zero does not mean globally identical.

title: Hilbert Obstruction
notes: Frame Hilbert's theorem as a warning about local models. Patches of constant negative curvature exist, but a complete regular surface in Euclidean three-space cannot realize that metric everywhere. Global completeness and extrinsic regularity collide with the curvature demand.

title: Topology Links
notes: This table gathers the lecture's repeated pattern. A local geometric measurement becomes powerful only after a global hypothesis selects the correct category of surfaces. Compactness, completeness, simple connectivity, and regular embedding each block a different escape route.

title: Sanity Checks And Takeaways
notes: Close by translating the lecture into tests the notebook can run. Check Gauss-Bonnet on model surfaces, verify angle defects on meshes, test Jacobi focusing signs, compare flat developments, and ask whether a claimed global surface violates completeness, topology, or embedding constraints.
